verdict: PARTIAL WIN, honestly. (a) The NATIVE / content-triggered decision to invoke the ALU works and generalizes with NO special mode (100% trigger recall, 0% false-trigger, inline == mode-gated -> a mode cue is unnecessary for triggering). (b) Language is preserved exactly (host frozen, delta 0). (c) The ALU stays byte-exact on whatever is routed (byte-exactness is never the failure). (d) The WALL is operand READING: the operand digits ARE recoverable and generalize at the exact token (units 84-100% held-out), but composing full multi-digit operands to byte-exact does NOT generalize out-of-distribution (0/60 disjoint range) and only 26% in-distribution held-out, because per-digit errors compound and higher-place digits do not extrapolate to unseen magnitudes. So: the network CAN natively/inline DECIDE to use the ALU without a special mode and keep language intact, but end-to-end byte-exact inline arithmetic on UNSEEN operands is NOT achieved by a frozen-host + trained-router here -- the honest cost is that operand extraction is the binding constraint, not the trigger and not the ALU.
precedent_positioning: Toolformer learns WHEN to call an external tool inline from text -> here the 'when' (trigger) likewise generalizes inline with no mode token, but the tool is an INTERNAL byte-exact constructed circuit (not a black-box API) and the failure is the NALU-style operand-VALUE generalization (reading/composing the number), which frozen-host+linear-router does not solve extrapolatively; DNC-style learned addressing to the digit tokens is what makes the per-digit read generalize (units 100%), but full-operand composition remains the wall.
